site.summary: microsoft-privacy-clone Clone of the Microsoft account privacy management panel and its sub-pages. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Main panel: top black Microsoft ribbon + account header (4-square logo + global nav + avatar); hero section with title and Privacy Checkup / Download / Privacy Statement entries; activity-data card grid (Browse / Search / Location / Voice / Media / Apps / Xbox / Ads — 8 cards total); privacy-settings toggle list (6 toggles with live "Saving…/Saved" feedback); two manage-data tiles (download / clear, clear has a modal second-confirmation); Microsoft product-level privacy entries (Windows / Xbox / Edge / Bing / Outlook / OneDrive / LinkedIn / M365) | | `browse-history.html` | Edge browse-history detail: breadcrumb, setting-status hint, filter bar (time range / device / search box), activity table (time / page title + URL / device / delete icon), per-row delete with animation, "Clear all" with modal confirmation, empty state | | `ad-settings.html` | Ad settings: master toggle (See ads that interest you) controls all sub-items; per-service cards (Microsoft / Bing & Edge / LinkedIn / Xbox) with independent toggles; multi-select intere

run_plan.goal: Autonomously explore the full Microsoft privacy management experience, centered on the privacy dashboard and the linked data-management flows for browse history, ad settings, and data download, including destructive actions, save feedback, filtering, and responsive behavior.
run_plan.summary: Start on the privacy dashboard to validate the main information architecture, linked destinations, and the inline privacy-setting controls with their save states. Then follow the strongest adjacent flows exposed by the prescan: browse history management, ad personalization controls, and the download-your-data request flow. Reserve dedicated attention for destructive or stateful interactions such as clear/delete confirmations, master-detail toggle dependencies, and any mobile usability issues already hinted by the prescan's small tap target warnings.
assumptions: Only four HTML pages are known and should define the exploration scope: index.html, browse-history.html, ad-settings.html, and download-data.html.
Several dashboard links appear to be placeholders (#) and should be checked for non-navigation or dead-end behavior rather than treated as full destination flows.
The dashboard includes 6 privacy-setting toggles with live "Saving…/Saved" feedback, which is a primary state-change interaction worth explicit validation.
browse-history.html contains per-row deletion, filtering, a clear-all confirmation modal, and an empty state based on the README/prescan.
ad-settings.html includes a master toggle that affects service-level personalization controls plus ad-topic multi-select interests.
download-data.html is a single-page form flow with category selection, time range, delivery method, and confirmation, not a multi-page wizard.
risk_hotspots: index.html: privacy-settings toggle list with live "Saving…/Saved" feedback may have timing/state consistency issues
index.html: manage-data clear tile and second-confirmation modal are destructive and need cancel/confirm coverage
index.html: multiple visible links with href="#" may create dead ends or misleading affordances
browse-history.html: per-row delete icon with animation may fail to remove rows cleanly or update counts/table state
browse-history.html: Clear all browse history modal is high risk for destructive confirmation and empty-state transition
browse-history.html: time-range/device filters plus search box may produce inconsistent table filtering or no-results handling
ad-settings.html: master toggle controlling all sub-items may create dependency, reversibility, or partial-state issues
ad-settings.html: service-level toggles may conflict with global state or become incorrectly enabled/disabled
ad-settings.html: ad-topic multi-select interests may have unclear selection feedback or persistence behavior
download-data.html: large set of checkboxes/radios and final request submission may have validation, summary, or completion-state issues
Global header/navigation on mobile: prescan already reports many small tap targets, so top nav and utility links need responsive scrutiny

phases.title: Dashboard baseline and primary entry points
phases.objective: Validate the privacy dashboard as the hub page, including content hierarchy, visible controls, and the main outbound paths into deeper privacy tasks.
key_checks: Confirm the dashboard loads with the expected major sections: hero, activity cards, privacy settings, and manage-your-data areas
Open the known working destinations from the dashboard: Download your data and Manage browse activity
Look for an entry to ad settings from the dashboard and use it if present; otherwise navigate directly later
Test visible hero/support actions that appear to use href="#" and note whether they do nothing, scroll, or mislead
Check whether the current Privacy tab in the account nav is clearly indicated and whether surrounding nav links appear interactive but nonfunctional
exit_criteria: Main dashboard structure and major sections are observed
All known linked destination pages have confirmed entry paths from the dashboard where available
Placeholder or dead-end links on the dashboard are identified with evidence

phases.title: Dashboard settings and destructive controls
phases.objective: Exercise the dashboard's inline stateful controls and destructive data-management actions, focusing on feedback clarity and reversibility.
key_checks: Toggle each of the 6 privacy settings at least once and verify visible state change plus the promised "Saving…/Saved" feedback
Toggle a setting repeatedly or in quick succession to see whether feedback stacks, stalls, or becomes ambiguous
Use the manage-data download tile/action and confirm it routes consistently to download-data.html
Trigger the dashboard clear-data flow if exposed, inspect the second-confirmation modal, and validate both cancel and confirm paths
After any destructive confirmation, verify whether surrounding copy, counts, or empty messaging reflect the action
exit_criteria: Most or all dashboard toggles have been exercised with save feedback observed
Destructive clear flow has both cancel and confirm coverage
Any post-action confirmation, state persistence, or mismatch issues are documented

phases.title: Browse history management flow
phases.objective: Validate the detailed activity-management experience for browse history, including filtering, item deletion, bulk clearing, and empty/no-results states.
key_checks: Verify breadcrumb/back navigation to the privacy dashboard
Change Time range and Device selections and observe whether the table contents or visible state updates coherently
Use the search box with matching and likely non-matching terms to probe filtering and no-results behavior
Delete at least one individual history row using the trash icon and verify animation, row removal, and any count/state update
Trigger Clear all browse history and validate modal wording, cancel path, confirm path, and resulting empty state
Check whether the page still communicates browse-history saving status and the Change this setting link behavior
exit_criteria: Filter controls and search input have been exercised with observable results
Single-item delete and bulk clear have both been tested
An empty or cleared state has been reached or the inability to reach it has been explicitly noted

phases.title: Ad personalization controls
phases.objective: Assess the clarity and behavior of ad-personalization settings, especially global-versus-local control relationships and topic selection affordances.
key_checks: Toggle the master "See ads that interest you" control and observe effects on service-level toggles/cards
Test at least two service-specific toggles both when the master setting is on and after changing the master setting
Check whether LinkedIn/Xbox/service cards communicate dependencies, disabled states, or contradictory combinations clearly
Interact with multiple ad-topic options and verify selection feedback for add/remove or multi-select behavior
Use breadcrumb/dashboard return navigation to confirm recoverability from this detail page
exit_criteria: Master toggle behavior relative to service-level controls is understood
Multiple service toggles and topic selections have been exercised
Any dependency confusion, unclear copy, or state inconsistency has been captured

phases.title: Download-your-data request and responsive pass
phases.objective: Complete the data export flow coverage and then repeat the highest-value interactions on mobile to assess responsiveness and tap usability.
key_checks: On download-data.html, test category selection patterns such as all/default versus a custom subset
Change the time-range option and delivery choice if multiple options are present
Proceed through the final confirmation/request action and verify any success, acknowledgement, or summary state
Check whether the form prevents invalid/incomplete submission if required selections are missing

Repeat critical mobile checks on all four pages: top navigation/header usability, dashboard toggles, browse-history filters/search/delete or clear modal, ad-settings master toggle, and download form controls
On mobile, specifically inspect controls already flagged in prescan for small tap targets and watch for wrapping, overlap, clipping, or horizontal scroll
exit_criteria: The download request flow has been taken as far as the UI allows with completion or validation feedback observed
A focused mobile pass has covered the main hub and each major detail flow
Responsive issues affecting task completion, readability, or tap accuracy are documented

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 4 known HTML pages and return to the dashboard from at least two detail pages to verify hub-and-spoke navigation.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise the main visible controls on each key page: dashboard toggles and clear/download actions, browse-history filters/search/per-row delete/clear-all modal, ad-settings master and service toggles plus topic selections, and most major download-data form inputs and final submission.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical task checks on a mobile viewport for all known pages, with special focus on header/nav tap targets, modals, toggles, filter controls, and form usability.

notes: Do not spend much of the budget on top-level account nav items like Home, Devices, Security, Rewards, or Order history unless they unexpectedly navigate within the known site; the prescan suggests many are placeholders.
Prioritize evidence-rich state transitions over link enumeration, since this clone appears strongest in inline settings, modal confirmations, and data-management interactions.
If a control appears present in README but is not easily discoverable in the DOM during execution, note the discoverability gap rather than assuming hidden capability.

ux_notes: Clicking "Clear all browse history" from an empty filtered state opens a confirmation modal with clear destructive wording ("This permanently removes every entry shown here") plus both Cancel and "Yes, clear all" actions, which supports trust and reversibility.

The modal explains scope as only the entries currently shown and notes that devices may keep local history until re-sign-in, but because the page simultaneously says "No browse activity matches the current filters," users may still wonder whether confirming would delete nothing or broader unseen history.

step.objective: Learn whether confirming Clear all browse history when no rows currently match filters gives clear post-action feedback and preserves user trust.
step.success_criteria: The modal closes and the page shows a clear resulting state, ideally indicating whether nothing was deleted or confirming completion without implying broader hidden deletion.

result.feedback: No obvious URL or visible-text change was detected after the action.

ux_notes: The mobile 'Clear all browse history' action opens a confirmation modal with a clear destructive title ('Clear all browse history?') and explanatory scope text stating it removes every entry shown from the Microsoft account while warning devices may retain local history until sign-in again.

The confirmation dialog presents both cancel and confirm choices as visible side-by-side buttons, but the original trigger is only 196x35px and flagged below 44px mobile guidance, indicating the destructive flow starts from a slightly undersized touch target.
Mobile layout still shows horizontal overflow (page width 480px vs viewport 390px) behind the modal, which can reduce trust and polish during a sensitive destructive action.

step.objective: Learn whether confirming mobile 'Clear all browse history' gives clear completion feedback, updates the list to an empty state, and preserves trust during a destructive action.
step.success_criteria: The modal closes and the page shows a clear cleared/empty state, reduced entries, or explicit completion feedback indicating what was deleted.

result.feedback: Visible content changed after the action.

ux_notes: The destructive confirmation modal is still open after tapping “Yes, clear all”; the heading “Clear all browse history?” and both actions “Cancel” and “Yes, clear all” remain visible, so there is no completion feedback yet.

The list behind the modal still shows existing history rows (for example “Maps — Shinjuku station” and “Stripe Docs — Hosted checkout quickstart”), so this action did not produce the expected empty state or visible reduction in entries.
On mobile, the page has horizontal overflow (479px content width on a 390px viewport), which can undermine confidence during a destructive flow by making the interface feel unstable or clipped.

step.objective: Learn whether the mobile clear-all confirmation still offers a reliable cancel/recovery path after the confirm action appears to fail.
step.success_criteria: The modal closes and the browse-history page becomes usable again without clearing entries, showing whether users can recover from a failed destructive confirmation.

ux_notes: The attempted mobile recovery path failed: clicking the modal's Cancel button timed out because the locator resolved but 'element is not visible,' so the UI did not provide a reliably accessible cancel action after the failed confirmation flow.

The page appears usable again and shows an empty-state message ('No browse activity matches the current filters') plus the main 'Clear all browse history' button in the interactables list, but because the cancel button could not be activated, this does not confirm a trustworthy recovery path.

On mobile, several relevant controls remain undersized for touch, including 'Clear all browse history' at 196x35 and 'Change this setting' at 305x35, reinforcing potential interaction difficulty around destructive/privacy settings actions.

step.objective: Learn whether the mobile breadcrumb-style 'Privacy dashboard' link is usable despite its undersized tap target and whether returning to the hub remains clear and confidence-building.
step.success_criteria: The app navigates to index.html and clearly reorients the user on the Privacy dashboard without confusion or layout breakage on mobile.
